questions.article: Science: A Means of Reinforcing Faith
questions.q: Many expected the advance of science to weaken religion. What is the editorial’s view of what has actually happened?
options: Religion has had to abandon its claims
Not quite. The article says: Modern knowledge has corroborated the truths of religion and strengthened faith in God.
Modern knowledge has corroborated the truths of religion and strengthened faith in God
Yes. “We shall show them Our signs in the universe and within themselves.”
Science has stopped asking large questions
Not quite. The article says: Modern knowledge has corroborated the truths of religion and strengthened faith in God.
Science and religion no longer concern each other
Not quite. The article says: Modern knowledge has corroborated the truths of religion and strengthened faith in God.
questions.rationale: “Far from having a damaging effect on religion, modern knowledge has served to corroborate and consolidate its truths.”

questions.article: The Scientific Approach of the Quran
questions.q: Which prayer of the Prophet does the article call a fine example of the scientific approach?
options: “Show us the truth as truth… show us falsehood as falsehood… Show us things as they are”
Right. Thinking in accordance with reality.
“Increase our wealth and our children”
Not quite. The article says: “Show us the truth as truth… show us falsehood as falsehood… Show us things as they are”.
“Grant us victory over our opponents”
Not quite. The article says: “Show us the truth as truth… show us falsehood as falsehood… Show us things as they are”.
“Make our journey short”
Not quite. The article says: “Show us the truth as truth… show us falsehood as falsehood… Show us things as they are”.
questions.rationale: “O God, show us the truth in the form of truth and grant us the wisdom to follow it… Show us things as they are.”

questions.article: The Scientific Approach of the Quran
questions.q: The Quran asks believers to “say the right word” (qaul-e-sadid). With what image does the article explain it?
options: A seed that grows slowly
Not quite. The article says: An arrow shot straight at its target – speech that matches the facts exactly.
A lamp that lights a room
Not quite. The article says: An arrow shot straight at its target – speech that matches the facts exactly.
An arrow shot straight at its target – speech that matches the facts exactly
Well read. Not conjecture or mere opinion.
A river that finds its level
Not quite. The article says: An arrow shot straight at its target – speech that matches the facts exactly.
questions.rationale: “Just as the arrow reaches its target by being shot in precisely the right direction, similarly qaul-e-sadid hits the mark by making one’s words correspond in every detail with reality.”

questions.q: In what sense did Einstein count himself among “devoutly religious men”?
options: In his belief that science has no limits
Not quite. The article says: In his conviction that a reality beyond our grasp exists, showing itself as the highest wisdom and beauty.
In his regular attendance at worship
Not quite. The article says: In his conviction that a reality beyond our grasp exists, showing itself as the highest wisdom and beauty.
In his study of ancient scriptures
Not quite. The article says: In his conviction that a reality beyond our grasp exists, showing itself as the highest wisdom and beauty.
In his conviction that a reality beyond our grasp exists, showing itself as the highest wisdom and beauty
Yes. Nature points beyond itself.
questions.rationale: “To know that what is impenetrable to us really exists, manifesting itself as the highest wisdom and the most radiant beauty… this feeling, is at the centre of true religiousness.”

questions.q: For ages men tried to turn iron into gold by secret formulas. What does the article say modern discovery achieved instead?
options: Gold was at last made from iron
Not quite. The article says: Iron is turned into machines more valuable than gold, by using nature’s real laws.
Iron is turned into machines more valuable than gold, by using nature’s real laws
Correct. Hence the modern mind trusts what is tested.
The old formulas were proved right
Not quite. The article says: Iron is turned into machines more valuable than gold, by using nature’s real laws.
Iron was found to be worthless
Not quite. The article says: Iron is turned into machines more valuable than gold, by using nature’s real laws.
questions.rationale: “Now, thanks to the discovery of natural realities, iron is converted into machines more precious than gold.”

questions.q: A leader once mocked that a spacecraft had found no God in space. How does the article reply with a finding of modern science?
options: Spacecraft have since travelled further
Not quite. The article says: Only a small part of the universe is observable to man, so direct observation cannot be demanded; God is known through His creation.
Space is too dark for cameras
Not quite. The article says: Only a small part of the universe is observable to man, so direct observation cannot be demanded; God is known through His creation.
Only a small part of the universe is observable to man, so direct observation cannot be demanded; God is known through His creation
Well reasoned. Indirect knowledge is the only kind available.
The claim was never really made
Not quite. The article says: Only a small part of the universe is observable to man, so direct observation cannot be demanded; God is known through His creation.
questions.rationale: “Only around four per cent of the vast universe is observable for man… man, given his present abilities, can arrive only at indirect knowledge about God.”

questions.q: In 2012 a huge solar eruption crossed Earth’s orbit but missed the planet, which was then on the far side of the sun. How does the article regard this “luck”?
options: As a warning to abandon electricity
Not quite. The article says: As a sign of the control and protection that govern the universe.
As proof that such storms are harmless
Not quite. The article says: As a sign of the control and protection that govern the universe.
As a sign of the control and protection that govern the universe
Right. “Who will save you… by night and by day?”
As an event of no significance
Not quite. The article says: As a sign of the control and protection that govern the universe.
questions.rationale: “What was this ‘luck’? In fact, it was an intervention by the Lord of the universe… there is a high control of check and balance in the universe.”

questions.q: How does the article see the discoveries of modern astronomy – expanding space, vast galaxies, giant black holes?
options: As enlarging our sense of God’s greatness and of our own smallness
Yes. “Hearts tremble with awe at the mention of God.”
As reasons for fear alone
Not quite. The article says: As enlarging our sense of God’s greatness and of our own smallness.
As making man the master of space
Not quite. The article says: As enlarging our sense of God’s greatness and of our own smallness.
As having no bearing on faith
Not quite. The article says: As enlarging our sense of God’s greatness and of our own smallness.
questions.rationale: “Scientific discoveries have truly enlarged the canvas of God-realization… These facts remind man of his state of extreme helplessness and the state of omnipotence of God.”

questions.q: When Moses’ staff became a serpent, what universal law does the article say was being shown?
options: The law of conversion – everything in nature is being changed from one form into another
Exactly. A seed into a tree, an egg into a chick.
The law that the strong overcome the weak
Not quite. The article says: The law of conversion – everything in nature is being changed from one form into another.
The law that wood outlasts stone
Not quite. The article says: The law of conversion – everything in nature is being changed from one form into another.
The law that nothing ever changes
Not quite. The article says: The law of conversion – everything in nature is being changed from one form into another.
questions.rationale: “Moses had demonstrated to people a universal and common law of God. This is the law of conversion.”

questions.q: We can calculate exactly how an arrow falls, yet not say why it returns to earth. What does the article conclude about the scope of science?
options: Science will soon answer every “why”
Not quite. The article says: Science describes how things happen; the meaning and purpose behind them come from revelation.
Such questions have no answers
Not quite. The article says: Science describes how things happen; the meaning and purpose behind them come from revelation.
Calculation is of little use
Not quite. The article says: Science describes how things happen; the meaning and purpose behind them come from revelation.
Science describes how things happen; the meaning and purpose behind them come from revelation
Well read. The two do not compete.
questions.rationale: “Science does not negate the Creator, as its goal is to understand and explain the natural phenomena. It makes no claim to account for the underlying reason of the events.”
